stress_625.why: The standing stress level (docs/scale-audit-2026-10-13.md section 5; made by docs/scale-audit-2026-10-13/make_stress_levels.sh, never committed): 625 x 625 terrain samples, 268 m a side, 3 copies of test_room and a wild tile with a mountain, a lake, a hut, 8 lamps and 4 fires. Its home tile IS test_room at test_room's own coordinates, so every view above is also a view of it: the same picture with 5.9 times the level behind it. A cost that moves between the two is a cost that follows the level, not the picture. These are the views only the large level has. `bench.py --level stress_625`; offline, `SCENE=stress_625 GAME_DIR=<the scratch game folder>`.

views.name: stress_field
views.note: test_room's outdoors_field, in the stress level: the same picture, 5.9 times the level. Read against outdoors_field on test_room: the difference is the per-frame work that follows the whole level.

views.note: 20 m in from a corner, looking at the middle: the longest sight line, the far sea, the sun map's texel on far walls (F3).

views.note: In front of the site one tile east (110 m from home), looking back at home's building: the one sun map's texel, the 16 lights chosen by distance, the buildings' reflection table, the model draw range (F3, F5, F6, F8).

views.name: stress_lamps
views.note: In the wild tile's lamp ring, across its lake: 8 lamps, 4 fires, the hut's lamps, the sun and (with a torch) its beam and bounce -- more than 16 lights in reach (F5): which are chosen, and whether they pop.

views.note: A 10 s walk at 3 m/s on a fixed line from the home hall's door toward the beach, then round and back: the rig moves every frame, so whatever is still re-posed or re-sent for the whole level shows here and in no standing view (F1).
